## TL;DR I walked Settings → General and Agents → Budget Controls headlessly in WebKit at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Neither page overflowed at any width, and both threw no page errors. The real problems were accessibility, not layout: most of the General tab's setting controls had no accessible name, because each row's label was a plain `div` with no link to its control. A few of the same controls had no visible focus change. I fixed the row pattern once, in `SettingsView.vue`, and added a Playwright probe (`src/ui-app/tests/settings-agents-budget-qa-browser.test.ts`) that walks both pages at all three widths. The probe passes on the rebuilt app. Loading, empty and error states, and wording review beyond control names, were not covered by this pass. ## Work and rationale Task #1263 asked for a sweep of the Settings General tab, the agents page and its budget tab for layout, wording, save and validation bugs, at three widths. The acceptance criteria require a headless walk, fixing every issue found across its whole class, and a scoped check. I read the `SettingsView.vue` outline and the existing notification QA test (`notifications-settings-qa-browser.test.ts`) as a template. Budget Controls is not a Settings tab: it lives on the Agents page, at `/agents?tab=budget-controls`, so I took "agents and budget" to mean that route. I took "Settings general" to mean `/settings?tab=general`. The existing `agents-page-qa-browser.test.ts` (#1223) covers the agent list, providers and routing tabs, but not Budget Controls, so that was new ground. The first probe flagged five classes of finding: 1. Setting controls with no accessible name. In `SettingsView.vue`, each generic setting row renders `
` next to the control, with no `for`/`id` link and no `aria-label` on the control. The boolean `Switch`, the text and number `Input`s and the `Select` triggers were therefore unnamed for screen readers. I added `:aria-label="f.label"` to those controls at the four config-driven row sites, and named the hand-written switches for glide animations, keyboard navigation, ntfy, Telegram, sound, push, per-type notifications and authentication from their row labels. 2. Focus changes. My first focus check used programmatic focus and read styles mid-transition, so the `Input` (which has `transition-colors`) looked unfocused. With transitions disabled inside the probe, the shared `Input`, `Select` trigger and `Switch` all show a real focus change, so I left the shared primitives alone. 3. False positives I removed from the probe. The floating assistant buttons are named by their ``, and the CTO safe-action checkboxes are named by their wrapping `
